title: Hilt (Dependency Injection)
objectives: Explain dependency injection and why it helps

sections.markdown: Hilt is a dependency-injection library built on Dagger that generates the wiring for you. DI means objects receive their dependencies instead of creating them, improving testability and decoupling.

rows: Tell Hilt how to build a type

sections.markdown: DI inverts control: instead of `UserRepository()` creating an `Api`, the Api is injected. In tests you inject a fake Api — no real network. This is the Dependency Inversion Principle in practice.
Scope deliberately: @Singleton for app-wide singletons, @ViewModelScoped for per-ViewModel. Over-scoping to @Singleton everywhere causes leaks and stale state.

flashcards.back: Objects receive their dependencies from outside instead of creating them — improving testability and decoupling.
Allows Hilt to inject dependencies into Android classes like Activities and Fragments.
When you can't @Inject a constructor (interfaces, third-party types) and must tell Hilt how to build it.
